title: Every Way to Abbreviate a Word

concept.title: Each letter is kept or skipped, and skipped runs become numbers
body: To abbreviate a word, you replace some **non-overlapping runs of consecutive letters** by the length of the run: `word` can become `w2d` (the two letters `or` are replaced by 2), `4`, `1o2`, and so on. Every letter has two possible fates: it is **kept**, or it is **skipped** (becomes part of a number). A run of skipped letters is written as one number.

The search walks along the word and remembers how many letters were skipped since the last kept letter. When a letter is kept, the pending number (if not zero) is written first, then the letter. At the end of the word, a pending number is written last.

body.code:
def abbr(w, pos, skipped, current, out):
    if pos == len(w):
        out.append("".join(current) + (str(skipped) if skipped else ""))
        return
    abbr(w, pos + 1, skipped + 1, current, out)                   # skip this letter
    current.append((str(skipped) if skipped else "") + w[pos])   # keep it
    abbr(w, pos + 1, 0, current, out)
    current.pop()

body: Every one of the `2^n` choices gives a different text, so no duplicate has to be removed. Digits have smaller codes than letters, so the sorted order puts the abbreviations that begin with a number first.

statement: Print all abbreviations of a word. An abbreviation is made by replacing any number of non-overlapping runs of consecutive letters with the length of the run (the replaced letters of one run become one number). Print the abbreviations in ascending order (digits come before letters; compare character by character), one per line.
inputFormat: The only line has the word of lowercase letters.
outputFormat: The `2^n` abbreviations in ascending order, one per line.

examples.note: The four abbreviations are 1b, 2, a1 and ab.

hints: Every letter is either kept or skipped: two calls per position.
Count the letters skipped in a row; write the count before the next kept letter, or at the end.
There are 2^n results and they are all different; sort them at the end.

explanation: Each letter is skipped (the run counter grows) or kept (the pending number is written, then the letter). At the end a pending number is written. The `2^n` texts are sorted.
solution.complexity: Time O(2^n * n), space O(n) besides the output.

code.python:
def abbr(w, pos, skipped, current, out):
    if pos == len(w):
        out.append("".join(current) + (str(skipped) if skipped else ""))
        return
    abbr(w, pos + 1, skipped + 1, current, out)
    current.append((str(skipped) if skipped else "") + w[pos])
    abbr(w, pos + 1, 0, current, out)
    current.pop()

word = input().strip()

out = []
abbr(word, 0, 0, [], out)
out.sort()
print("\n".join(out))
